scope: Non-operational structural/computational hypothesis audit only. No wet-lab protocol, pathogen engineering, or clinical treatment claim.
original_candidate_law: Directional genome egress in an icosahedral RNA virion is anchored either by a dedicated portal/unique structural vertex or by asymmetric cargo-shell contact topology.

falsifying_witness.result: Published work supports a third symmetry-breaking route: membrane/receptor proximity can induce a unique local capsid remodeling event in a previously symmetric particle, and authors explicitly favor a stochastic induced-asymmetry model over a required pre-existing weak spot.
falsifying_witness.why_it_breaks_duality: A unique egress site need not be pre-encoded as a dedicated portal and need not be proven to originate from pre-existing cargo-shell topology; host-context-induced local symmetry breaking is a distinct causal class.

prior_art_pressure.review_level_result: Reviews of icosahedral-virus asymmetry already distinguish inherent asymmetry from asymmetry that develops during the viral life cycle and note that genome release can use a preformed portal or create one.

preserved_value: The failed hypothesis is retained as a falsification witness proving that JANUS must permit intrinsic structural, cargo-encoded, and context-induced symmetry breaking without forcing a closed taxonomy.
